Databricks lists about 580 customer case-study pages on its site, and Snowflake lists 225. Of those, 101 Databricks pages and 40 Snowflake case studies are in financial services. These counts are as of 2026-10-19 and come from each site's own customer listing, with the financial-services filter applied. The two sites count things differently, so the totals aren't directly comparable.

## Counts

| | Databricks | Snowflake |
|---|---|---|
| Listing total | 952 "customers" | 390 stories (225 case studies, plus videos and snapshots) |
| Published case-study pages | about 580 (579 distinct URLs, 528 companies) | 225 |
| Financial services | 101 pages | 40 case studies |

- **Databricks:** most of the 952 entries are logo-only cards or link to a blog post or video rather than a case-study page. I counted only the cards that link to a `databricks.com/customers/...` page. Some companies have several pages, such as Banco Bradesco, Coinbase and NAB. The filter shows 146 financial-services entries; the other 45 are logos, blogs or videos with no case-study page. That 579 figure is a count from scraping the 49 listing pages, so treat it as accurate to within a few.
- **Snowflake:** the 225 comes straight from the site's "Case Study" filter. Its financial-services filter shows 40 case studies. That count excludes videos and snapshots, which the same industry filter would add to.
- **Industry tags:** I used each site's own financial-services tag. Some tagged items are only loosely financial. Snowflake's Foodics is a restaurant-software story, and Databricks' CZ is a healthcare insurer, CPEX is ad targeting, JLL is real estate, and Quantum Capital is energy deals.

I found a solid entry for three of the five. Zed is only partly confirmed, and I couldn't find a JetBrains changelog entry at all.

| Tool | Version | Date | Entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| **VS Code (Copilot)** | 1.99 | Mar 2025 | https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_model-context-protocol-server-support |
| **Windsurf** | 1.3.3 | Feb 13, 2025 | https://windsurf.com/changelog (see caveat) |
| **Cursor** | 0.45.x (MCP added in 0.45.6) | Jan 23, 2025 (entry date) | https://cursor.com/changelog/0-45-x |
| **Zed** | v0.152.0-pre (stable v0.152.3) | Sep 4, 2024 (pre) / Sep 10, 2024 (stable) | https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/releases/tag/v0.152.0-pre |
| **JetBrains AI Assistant** | 2025.1 | Not found | Not found |

**VS Code:** The 1.99 notes have a dedicated "Model Context Protocol server support" section. I'm confident in the section anchor. The page shows only the month, so I don't have an exact day for you. If you need one, the release was around April 3, 2025, because GitHub's changelog post about it is dated April 3.

**Windsurf:**
- The 1.3.3 entry (Feb 13, 2025) says "Cascade now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP)". I read it in a Wayback Machine snapshot from 2025, not on the live site.
- The live windsurf.com/changelog now redirects to docs.devin.ai and only goes back to 1.6.1.
- For a stable link, use the archive URL: `https://web.archive.org/web/20250301000000/https://windsurf.com/changelog`, and look for the 1.3.3 section.

**Cursor:**
- The page is cursor.com/changelog/0-45-x, dated Jan 23, 2025. The MCP line is in an "UPDATE (0.45.1–0.45.11)" note added after the original entry: "Also adds MCP support…".
- The text doesn't say 0.45.6. That number comes from a Cursor forum changelog thread and a Reddit post, so cite it as 0.45.x unless you accept that source.
- The MCP line was added after Jan 23, so the first mention is probably a few days later. I didn't pin down that date.

**Zed:**
- The earliest release notes mentioning "context servers" are v0.152.0-pre and v0.152.3. They only add prompt-argument completions and a panic fix for context servers.
- Zed's own name for MCP at the time was "context servers", and the notes don't use the word "MCP" there. The feature itself predates this release, but I didn't find its first introduction.
- The first release notes that literally say "MCP" that I found are v0.182.9-pre (Apr 15, 2025). They say "Improved compatibility when using MCPs with Gemini models", which is a bug fix, not an announcement.
- Zed's public MCP announcement was a blog post on Nov 25, 2024, which you said not to use.
- I searched GitHub release bodies. Zed's own zed.dev/releases pages didn't resolve for old versions.
- Decide which of the two framings (context servers in Sep 2024 or literal MCP in Apr 2025) fits your timeline.

**JetBrains:**
- The sources I found say the MCP client arrived with AI Assistant 2025.1, which is April 2025. Those are a YouTrack support article, JetBrains' MCP docs page and a blog post, and none of them is a changelog entry.
- I couldn't find or load an official AI Assistant release-notes page with a per-entry URL, and the Marketplace versions page returned nothing useful.
- Don't cite 2025.1 as a changelog entry until you've checked the plugin's "What's New" in an IDE or on the Marketplace page.

I scraped all 342 method pages linked from the Slack docs method index and read the "Rate Limits" line on each. The index page doesn't show tiers, so I had to fetch every page.

One fetch returned a 404 (`slacklists.access.set`). A retry showed Tier 3, so I counted it as Tier 3. The index has about 378 links, but they include duplicates, and 342 unique method pages is what I scraped.

## Tier 1 (1+ per minute): 17 methods
- `admin.apps.uninstall`
- `admin.conversations.restrictaccess.removegroup`
- `admin.teams.create`
- `admin.usergroups.addchannels`
- `admin.usergroups.create`
- `admin.usergroups.fetch`
- `admin.usergroups.update`
- `admin.users.unsupportedversions.export`
- `apps.icon.set`
- `apps.manifest.create`
- `apps.manifest.delete`
- `apps.manifest.update`
- `apps.uninstall`
- `conversations.listconnectinvites`
- `rtm.connect`
- `rtm.start` (deprecated)
- `team.externalteams.disconnect`

## "Special rate limits apply": 18 methods
- **Chat and search:** `chat.postMessage`, `chat.getPermalink`, `assistant.search.context`, `assistant.threads.setStatus`
- **Agents:** `agents.conversations.archive`, `.create`, `.listViews`, `.removeView`, `.setCommands`, `.setProperties`, `.setView`
- **Auth and OAuth:** `auth.test`, `oauth.v2.access`, `oauth.v2.user.access`, `tooling.tokens.rotate`
- **Other:** `admin.analytics.messages.metadata`, `apps.event.authorizations.list`, `blocks.validate`

`chat.postMessage` is the most likely culprit if you're posting messages. Slack's page doesn't give a tier for it. The rate-limits doc describes it as roughly 1 message per second per channel, with short bursts allowed.

## conversations.* methods (all `conversations.*` pages, 28 methods)
| Tier | Methods |
|---|---|
| **1** | `listConnectInvites` |
| **2** (20+/min) | `acceptSharedInvite`, `archive`, `canvases.create`, `close`, `create`, `externalInvitePermissions.set`, `inviteShared`, `list`, `rename`, `requestSharedInvite.approve`, `requestSharedInvite.deny`, `requestSharedInvite.list`, `setPurpose`, `setTopic`, `unarchive` |
| **3** (50+/min) | `approveSharedInvite`, `declineSharedInvite`, `history`, `info`, `invite`, `join`, `kick`, `leave`, `mark`, `open`, `replies` |
| **4** (100+/min) | `members` |

- **`conversations.history` and `conversations.replies`:** The page says that since May 29, 2025, non-Marketplace apps distributed commercially get 1 request per minute and a maximum of 15 objects per call. Only Marketplace and internal customer-built apps get Tier 3. The page header still shows Tier 3. If you're hitting limits on these two and your app is neither Marketplace nor internal, this is probably why. I only read this note on the `conversations.history` page, and I didn't check whether `conversations.replies` has the same one.
- **Related methods:** `users.conversations` is Tier 3. The `agents.conversations.*` methods are mostly "special", except `getCanvas` and `setCanvasContent` (Tier 3). The `admin.conversations.*` methods are mostly Tier 2, with `removegroup` at Tier 1 and `getTeams` and `setConversationPrefs` at Tier 3.

## Deprecated (marked on their own page)
- `rtm.start` is marked deprecated, with a link to the 2021 changelog. Use `rtm.connect` instead.
- `users.setActive` is described as "Deprecated and non-functional."

Other legacy methods like `files.upload`, `search.all`, `stars.*` and `oauth.access` don't carry a deprecation marker on their pages, so I didn't flag them.

## Tier summary (all methods)
| Tier | Methods |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 17 |
| Tier 2 | 171 |
| Tier 3 | 102 |
| Tier 4 | 33 |
| Special | 18 |

The full per-method list is in `/tmp/fceval-c1-t1-jkr7bmpk/work/.firecrawl/tiers.txt`. It lists `slacklists.access.set` as NONE because it holds the original 404 fetch.

**Things to know before emailing**
- **Not current faculty:** Clifton is emeritus. Bareinboim, Honorio and Shahbaz are adjunct, so they may not take Purdue students. Bareinboim's page is for his Columbia lab.
- **Counts:** Many come from a lab or team subpage, not the homepage. Several pages are undated or stale (Rompf, Goldwasser, Yexiang Xue). Where the page doesn't separate PhD students from postdocs or MS students, I say so.
- **Gaps:**
  - Campbell's 2025 paper wasn't looked up.
  - Zhang's EMNLP paper and Xiao's ICML paper have no full title on their pages.
  - Seven people have no 2025 paper on their pages: Clifton, Goldwasser, Jeong, Li, Neville, Rompf and Ruizhe Zhang. Valiant's newest paper on his page is from 2023.
- **Closest fits for ML/NLP:** Several people listed under the AI/ML/NLP category work mainly in systems, theory or robotics. Those papers are marked in the table.
- **Not included:** Vaneet Aggarwal (courtesy appointment) has no research areas listed in the directory, so I left him out. If you want him, his work is ML-heavy.
